title: Hook Hop – Free One-Button Jungle Swinging Game
description: Play Hook Hop free in your browser: hold to grab a vine, release to fly. Swing a cheeky monkey through the jungle, catch bananas and stay out of the river.
body: Hold to grab a vine, release to let go and fly. Swing a cheeky little monkey from knot to knot across an endless jungle, catching bananas in mid-air, and try not to splash into the river below.

Cracked vines snap a moment after you grab them, red mushrooms bounce you back up, and the knots drift farther apart the further you go. One button, no text, runs of one to three minutes, and it works on phones, tablets, Chromebooks and desktops. Your best distance and your banana total are saved automatically.
New here? Read how to play and the tips for longer swings.

title: How to Play Hook Hop – Controls, Vines, Mushrooms and Bananas
description: Hook Hop controls in one line: hold to grab the vine, release to fly. Learn how the white ring, cracked vines, mushrooms and bananas work.
body: Hook Hop uses a single input. Hold the mouse button, your finger or the Space bar to grab a vine knot and swing. Release to let go and fly with the speed you built up.

When you are in the air, a white ring marks the knot you will grab if you hold now: the nearest one ahead of the monkey and within reach. If there is no ring, nothing is close enough yet, so keep flying.
Each press grabs once. If you miss, or a vine snaps, release and press again to grab the next knot. While you hang, the swing builds up speed by itself at the bottom of the arc.

Pale, cracked knots are fragile. They creak, change colour and snap about a second and a half after you grab them (less later on). Red mushrooms by the river bounce you high into the air. Bananas float along the best swinging lines; touch them to collect them.
Your score is the distance in metres. The run ends when the monkey falls into the river. Once per run you can watch an optional ad to get back on the last good vine.

title: Hook Hop Tips: Longer Swings, Higher Flights, More Bananas
description: Seven practical tips to beat your best distance in Hook Hop: when to let go, how to handle cracked vines, using mushrooms and catching bananas.
body: Let go on the way up. The best moment to release is just after the lowest point, when the monkey is rising in front of the knot. Release at the bottom and you fly flat; release too late and you fly straight up.
Grab on the way down. Wait until the monkey starts to fall before you hold again. Grabbing while still climbing gives you a short, slow swing.
Long ropes are faster. Grabbing a knot from far away gives a long vine and a big, fast arc. Grabbing one right above your head gives a tight little circle.
Do not hang around on cracked knots. Grab, swing through the bottom once and let go. If it snaps under you, press again straight away to catch the next knot.
Mushrooms are a second chance. If you are too low, aim for a red mushroom: it throws you back up towards the vines.
High bananas pay off. The banana arcs up near the canopy are for players who let go at the right time. Chasing them also gives you more height for the next big gap.
Watch for the white ring. It always shows which knot you will catch. If it is on a cracked knot, be ready to let go quickly.

title: Hook Hop FAQ
description: Answers about Hook Hop: is it free, does it save, does it work on mobile and Chromebook, why did my vine snap, what are bananas for.
body: Is it free? Yes, it is free to play in the browser. There are no purchases.
Does it save my progress? Yes. Your best distance and the total number of bananas you have collected are stored in your browser (or in your account on portals that offer one).
Does it work on phones and Chromebooks? Yes. It runs in any modern browser, on touch screens and with a mouse or keyboard, in landscape or portrait. The download is about 1.6 MB.
Why did my vine snap? You grabbed a fragile knot: the pale, cracked ones. They break a moment after you grab them, and they get more common the further you go.
Why can't I grab anything? A knot must be ahead of the monkey and close enough. When one is in reach, a white ring appears on it. Each press grabs once, so release and press again after a miss.
What are bananas for? They are your collection: the menu shows how many you have gathered over all your runs. Try to beat your record of bananas in a single run too.
How long is a run? Usually one to three minutes. Restarting takes one click.

title: Hook Hop for Schools and Kids – Safe, Short, No Sign-up
description: Hook Hop is a short, text-free swinging game that works on school Chromebooks: no chat, no purchases, no account, no personal data.
h1: Hook Hop for classrooms and kids
body: Hook Hop has no chat, no purchases, no account and no personal data. Runs last one to three minutes, which makes it a good short reward between tasks.
There is no text in the game, only numbers and pictures, so it works the same for children who are still learning to read and for students of any language.

It is a playful way to feel how a pendulum works: a longer rope swings in a bigger arc, speed is highest at the bottom, and the moment you let go decides where you land. Timing the release is a small lesson in prediction and patience.
It runs in the browser on Chromebooks, tablets and phones and loads in a couple of seconds (about 1.6 MB). The monkey never gets hurt: falling just means a splash in the river and a fresh start.
